newsitem.title: UK: "Blushing bride" Branson launches wedding store.
newsitem.headline: "Blushing bride" Branson launches wedding store.

text.p: Millionaire British entreprenuer Richard Branson turned "drag queen" on Tuesday as he donned a white wedding dress and veil to celebrate the launch of his new store for wedding couples.
Branson shaved off his beard for the first time in 30 years as he made a surprise catwalk appearance at the end of a fashion show to publicise the Virgin Bride shop in the heart of London.

"Virgin Bride will change the way families organise weddings in the UK. It will be the largest bridal retail outlet in Europe, a one stop mecca for the great day," said Branson, who threw red roses into the crowd and flashed off his white fishnet stockings for photographers.
Branson's Virgin Group is one of Britain's largest private companies, ranging from financial services and rock music to airlines.

The new store is the brainchild of former Virgin Atlantic flight attendant Ailsa Petchey. She proposed the idea of a one-stop shop for brides to Branson after a frustrating time helping a friend to organise a wedding.
The store offers wedding dresses starting at a price of 700 pounds ($1,170) dollars, with informal gowns in the 300-700 pound price range.
Men's wear is provided by the costume designers for the hit movie "Four Weddings And A Funeral", with the accent on colourful waist coats and jackets.

Customers will be assigned a consultant on their first visit to the store who will assist them on all their plans. They will also be able to book their honeymoon through Virgin Bride, choose stationery and visit an in-store hair and beauty salon. ($1=.5995 Pound)
